html:
Natural draft cooling tower
Shell = surface of revolution of the hyperbola
x²/30² − y²/120² = 1
(a = 30 m waist radius, b = 120 m)
diameter = 60.0 m
Minimum span (60 m) occurs exactly at the waist, 100 m above ground. Below 8 m the shell is open — only the short splayed legs stand there.
View
Guided steps
The figure starts head-on, exactly as printed. Drag to orbit and every marked diameter turns into a full circle. Scroll to zoom, “Reset View” returns to the elevation.
⚠ Figure failed to load

plan.contextChunk: This figure is a dimensioned elevation drawing of a natural draft cooling tower, rendered as a translucent orange solid of revolution. The silhouette is widest at ground level, sweeps inward to a narrow waist above the midpoint, then flares slightly outward again to a flat circular top. The left half of the shell carries many closely spaced vertical contour lines following the curvature, while the right half is left as a smooth tinted surface, and a row of small teal angled supports rings the open base. A vertical dashed line runs up the center as the axis, and a horizontal dashed line crosses it at the waist. Four measurements are marked with double-headed arrows: 72 m across the top rim, 60 m across the narrow waist, 79.6 m from the top down to the waist level, and 179.6 m for the full height from ground to top, drawn along a long dimension line at the far left. Placing both diameters and both heights against the same profile makes the whole shape recoverable from four numbers. The layout supplies the data for fitting a hyperbola, centered where the dashed lines intersect, to the curved sides of the tower.

elements: Translucent orange solid of revolution: hyperboloid shell of a natural draft cooling tower, standing on the ground plane, widest at the base, narrowing to a waist, flaring slightly out to a flat circular top rim
Flat circular top rim (72 m diameter) drawn as the upper edge of the shell
Narrow circular waist (60 m diameter) at 100 m above ground (79.6 m below the top)
Closely spaced vertical meridian contour lines covering the LEFT half of the shell only, following the curvature from base to top
Smooth untextured tinted surface on the RIGHT half of the shell
Vertical dashed center line (axis of revolution) running the full height of the tower
Horizontal dashed line crossing the axis at the waist level, spanning the waist diameter
Ring of small teal angled supports (short splayed legs) around the open base of the shell, sitting on the ground line
Horizontal ground line at the tower base
Dimension arrow '72 m' with double-headed arrow and extension ticks above the top rim
Dimension arrow '60 m' with double-headed arrow across the waist (on the dashed waist line)
Vertical dimension arrow '79.6 m' with double-headed arrow from top rim level down to waist level, placed just left of the tower
Vertical dimension arrow '179.6 m' with double-headed arrow from ground to top rim, placed far left on a long dimension line
Movable horizontal measurement chord with double-headed arrow and live diameter readout (interactive element added to the figure)

interactions.teaches: How the tower's diameter varies with vertical position: the measuring chord shrinks to its 60 m minimum exactly at the waist and grows above and below it, tracing the hyperbolic profile
interactions.label: Measurement height above ground (m)

demo_steps.title: The dimensioned elevation
demo_steps.narration: The cooling tower is shown head-on: 179.6 m tall, 72 m across the flat top, and pinched to a 60 m waist 79.6 m below the top. The dashed lines mark the axis and the waist level.

demo_steps.title: Measuring at the waist
demo_steps.narration: Slide the measuring chord to 100 m above ground and it reaches its shortest span, 60 m — the narrowest circle of the tower and the vertex distance of the hyperbola.

demo_steps.title: Above and below the waist
demo_steps.narration: Move the chord up to the 179.6 m rim and it reads 72 m; drop it toward the ground and it widens again. The width grows symmetrically in both directions away from the waist.

demo_steps.title: The fitted hyperbola
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the profile view: the side of the tower is the branch pair of x²/30² − y²/120² = 1, centered where the axis meets the waist line. The 72 m width at y = 79.6 m is what forces b = 120.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Work in meters, then scale the whole scene by 1/40 for rendering (tower ≈4.5 world units tall). Origin at the center of the waist circle: ground plane at y = −100 m, top rim at y = +79.6 m, total height 179.6 m. Profile (radius as a function of height y measured from the waist, y in [−100, +79.6]): r(y) = 30·sqrt(1 + y²/120²), i.e. the hyperbola x²/30² − y²/120² = 1 with a = 30 m (waist radius, 60 m diameter) and b = 120 m. Check values: r(79.6) = 36 m → 72 m top diameter (exact by construction); r(−100) = 39.05 m → ≈78 m base diameter. The source drawing stylizes the base flare wider than this; render the true hyperbola but let the ring of splayed teal legs (each ~8 m tall, tilted ~20° outward, 16–20 of them evenly spaced around the base circle) carry the extra visual spread so the silhouette still reads as a flared cooling tower. Surface of revolution built as a lathe of the profile, translucent orange fill #F7C6A5 at ~0.45 opacity with silhouette/edge strokes #E07B43. Left half of the shell (screen-left, azimuth −90°..+90° on the near-left side) carries ~18 thin vertical meridian lines in #E8845A at 0.7 opacity; right half left smooth. Top rim drawn as a crisp ellipse/line in #E07B43. Teal supports #5FA8A3 with darker outline #3E8481. Dashed center axis (vertical, full height) and dashed waist chord in #E07B43 dashes. Dimension lines, arrowheads and text in dark gray #333333, text ~sans-serif: '72 m' centered above the top rim with short vertical extension ticks at ±36 m; '60 m' on the dashed waist chord with arrowheads at ±30 m; '79.6 m' on a vertical dimension line placed just left of the tower (about x = −45 m), running from top-rim level down to waist level; '179.6 m' on a long vertical dimension line far to the left (about x = −110 m), running ground to top rim. The interactive measuring chord is a horizontal double-headed arrow spanning ±r(y) at the slider height, colored #1B6CA8, with a live '{d} m' readout beside it. In 'Hyperbola profile' mode hide the lathed solid, the contour lines and the supports, and draw instead the 2D side curve (both branches, x = ±r(y)) as a bold #E07B43 stroke, plus the center point at the waist, the two asymptotes y = ±(120/30)x as thin gray dashed lines, and keep all four dimension arrows and the measuring chord.
interactionPlan.notes: Build the shell with THREE.LatheGeometry from ~120 profile samples of r(y) (MeshPhysicalMaterial, transparent, opacity ~0.45, side: DoubleSide, depthWrite false so the far wall shows through). Overlay meridian contours as LineSegments generated from the same profile at fixed azimuths, clipped to the left half by only emitting azimuths in the near-left range; keep them as Line2/thin tubes so they stay visible at 1px. Dimension lines, arrowheads, dashes and labels should be drawn as screen-facing sprites/HTML overlays anchored to projected 3D points so text stays upright and crisp while orbiting. The measuring chord updates by recomputing r(y) from the slider value each frame — no geometry rebuild, just reposition the line endpoints and re-render the readout. Toggle to 'Hyperbola profile' by fading the lathe opacity to 0 and cross-fading in a flat Line curve drawn in the z = 0 plane, snapping the camera back to azimuth 0 / elevation 0 during the transition. Soft hemisphere + single directional light; no shadows; white background to match the textbook figure.

authoredContext:
The design layout of a cooling tower is shown in the figure. The tower stands 179.6 meters tall. The diameter of the top is 72 meters. At their closest, the sides of the tower are 60 meters apart.

Project design for a natural draft cooling tower

A diagram illustrating the dimensions of a hyperbolic cooling tower, showing a total height of 179.6 m, an upper section height of 79.6 m, an upper diameter of 72 m, and a narrower waist diameter of 60 m.

Find the equation of the hyperbola that models the sides of the cooling tower. Assume that the center of the hyperbola—indicated by the intersection of dashed perpendicular lines in the figure—is the origin of the coordinate plane. Round final values to four decimal places.

discrepancies: Base flare is much weaker than in the source: the source silhouette widens dramatically toward the ground (base roughly twice the top width), whereas the generated lathe (r=39 m at ground vs 36 m at top) is nearly cylindrical below the waist, changing the characteristic cooling-tower silhouette at a glance.

The source shows meridian/contour striping only on the left half of the shell with the right half left as a smooth shaded surface; the generated striping reads as thin vertical lines spread across the whole visible front, losing the source's left/right contrast.
Duplicate waist annotation: both a black '60 m' dimension label and a blue '60.0 m' measuring readout sit on the same chord, cluttering the spot where the source has a single '60 m'.

The orange ground line extends well to the right beyond the tower base (and left under the dimension), an element not present in the source, where the ground/base line is confined to the tower footprint.
Teal base supports in the generated ring are thin, sparse pegs; in the source they are clearly drawn as splayed, outlined columns with visible box faces sitting under the flared shell edge.
evaluation.notes: A mathematically correct hyperboloid-of-revolution rendering of the dimensioned cooling tower with all four dimension callouts, a working measuring-chord slider, a hyperbola-profile toggle and guided steps; main weaknesses are the under-flared base compared with the source silhouette, duplicated waist labels, and an over-extended ground line.
action_items: Exaggerate or extend the lower profile (or lower the modeled ground plane/adjust drawn flare) so the base visibly widens like the source silhouette, while keeping the stated 60/72 m dimensions accurate.
Suppress the static black '60 m' label when the measuring readout sits at the waist (or offset one of them) to avoid duplicate text on the same chord.
Trim the ground line to the tower footprint and thicken/outline the teal base supports so they read as splayed columns like the source.
Restrict meridian contour lines to the left half of the shell so the left-striped / right-shaded contrast of the source is reproduced.

Dimension lines, arrowheads, dashes and labels should be drawn as screen-facing sprites/HTML overlays anchored to projected 3D points so text stays upright and crisp while orbiting. The measuring chord updates by recomputing r(y) from the slider value each frame — no geometry rebuild, just reposition the line endpoints and re-render the readout. Toggle to 'Hyperbola profile' by fading the lathe opacity to 0 and cross-fading in a flat Line curve drawn in the z = 0 plane, snapping the camera back to azimuth 0 / elevation 0 during the transition. Soft hemisphere + single directional light; no shadows; white background to match the textbook figure.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure is a dimensioned elevation drawing of a natural draft cooling tower, rendered as a translucent orange solid of revolution. The silhouette is widest at ground level, sweeps inward to a narrow waist above the midpoint, then flares slightly outward again to a flat circular top. The left half of the shell carries many closely spaced vertical contour lines following the curvature, while the right half is left as a smooth tinted surface, and a row of small teal angled supports rings the open base. A vertical dashed line runs up the center as the axis, and a horizontal dashed line crosses it at the waist. Four measurements are marked with double-headed arrows: 72 m across the top rim, 60 m across the narrow waist, 79.6 m from the top down to the waist level, and 179.6 m for the full height from ground to top, drawn along a long dimension line at the far left. Placing both diameters and both heights against the same profile makes the whole shape recoverable from four numbers. The layout supplies the data for fitting a hyperbola, centered where the dashed lines intersect, to the curved sides of the tower.
plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for height along the tower axis: the learner drags a horizontal measurement line from base to top and the current diameter updates against the curved side, making clear how the radius changes with vertical position on the hyperbolic profile.
- Toggle between full tower and fitted hyperbola profile: the learner switches from the translucent solid of revolution to the 2D side curve with the 60 m waist, 72 m top, and height marks, making clear how the four dimensions determine the model.

discrepancies: Base supports are far more prominent than in the source: 20 large splayed boxes ringing (and protruding well outside) the base rim, whereas the source shows a short row of small, slender teal columns tucked directly under the base line.

Slight camera elevation (4°) turns the flat top rim, waist chord and ground line into visible ellipses; the source is a strictly head-on elevation where those read as straight horizontal lines, so the composition is a touch less 'drawing-like'.

Meridian hatch lines in the source are confined to the left half of the shell and are dense, evenly spaced vertical curves; here they read as a sparse shaded band and the left/right asymmetry of the source fill (hatched left, plain right) is only loosely reproduced.
The static '60 m' waist label is hidden and replaced by the blue interactive readout '60.0 m' with a different colour/placement than the black '60 m' dimension of the source.
Added elements not in the source (equation text panel, asymptotes, hyperbola-profile mode, centre dot) — pedagogically useful but behind a toggle, adding chrome beyond the original figure.
evaluation.notes: A faithful and well-dimensioned 3D hyperboloid revolution of the textbook cooling-tower elevation with excellent interactions (measurement chord slider, profile toggle, guided steps); the main weaknesses are the oversized, over-splayed base columns that dominate the bottom of the figure and a small camera tilt that ellipticalises the otherwise head-on drawing.

Restore a black '60 m' dimension label on the dashed waist chord in the default state (keep the blue live readout offset elsewhere) so the four source dimensions read identically at first glance.

demo_steps.title: The dimensioned elevation
demo_steps.narration: The cooling tower is shown head-on: 179.6 m tall, 72 m across the flat top, and pinched to a 60 m waist 79.6 m below the top. The dashed lines mark the axis and the waist level.

demo_steps.title: Measuring at the waist
demo_steps.narration: Slide the measuring chord to 100 m above ground and it reaches its shortest span, 60 m — the narrowest circle of the tower and the vertex distance of the hyperbola.

demo_steps.title: Above and below the waist
demo_steps.narration: Move the chord up to the 179.6 m rim and it reads 72 m; drop it toward the ground and it widens again. The width grows symmetrically in both directions away from the waist.

demo_steps.title: The fitted hyperbola
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the profile view: the side of the tower is the branch pair of x²/30² − y²/120² = 1, centered where the axis meets the waist line. The 72 m width at y = 79.6 m is what forces b = 120.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Work in meters, then scale the whole scene by 1/40 for rendering (tower ≈4.5 world units tall). Origin at the center of the waist circle: ground plane at y = −100 m, top rim at y = +79.6 m, total height 179.6 m. Profile (radius as a function of height y measured from the waist, y in [−100, +79.6]): r(y) = 30·sqrt(1 + y²/120²), i.e. the hyperbola x²/30² − y²/120² = 1 with a = 30 m (waist radius, 60 m diameter) and b = 120 m. Check values: r(79.6) = 36 m → 72 m top diameter (exact by construction); r(−100) = 39.05 m → ≈78 m base diameter. The source drawing stylizes the base flare wider than this; render the true hyperbola but let the ring of splayed teal legs (each ~8 m tall, tilted ~20° outward, 16–20 of them evenly spaced around the base circle) carry the extra visual spread so the silhouette still reads as a flared cooling tower. Surface of revolution built as a lathe of the profile, translucent orange fill #F7C6A5 at ~0.45 opacity with silhouette/edge strokes #E07B43. Left half of the shell (screen-left, azimuth −90°..+90° on the near-left side) carries ~18 thin vertical meridian lines in #E8845A at 0.7 opacity; right half left smooth. Top rim drawn as a crisp ellipse/line in #E07B43. Teal supports #5FA8A3 with darker outline #3E8481. Dashed center axis (vertical, full height) and dashed waist chord in #E07B43 dashes. Dimension lines, arrowheads and text in dark gray #333333, text ~sans-serif: '72 m' centered above the top rim with short vertical extension ticks at ±36 m; '60 m' on the dashed waist chord with arrowheads at ±30 m; '79.6 m' on a vertical dimension line placed just left of the tower (about x = −45 m), running from top-rim level down to waist level; '179.6 m' on a long vertical dimension line far to the left (about x = −110 m), running ground to top rim. The interactive measuring chord is a horizontal double-headed arrow spanning ±r(y) at the slider height, colored #1B6CA8, with a live '{d} m' readout beside it. In 'Hyperbola profile' mode hide the lathed solid, the contour lines and the supports, and draw instead the 2D side curve (both branches, x = ±r(y)) as a bold #E07B43 stroke, plus the center point at the waist, the two asymptotes y = ±(120/30)x as thin gray dashed lines, and keep all four dimension arrows and the measuring chord.

discrepancies: The source is a flat orthographic elevation (top rim and waist read as straight lines); the generated view uses a perspective camera so the 72 m top rim and the base rim appear as pronounced ellipses, making the tower look tilted/seen from below rather than 'exactly as printed'.

The base flare and the leg ring are noticeably wider/more splayed than the source: the source shows a modest skirt with a horizontal ledge line and a single row of ~10 small teal blocks, while the generated version shows 18 legs spread across a large elliptical footprint that dominates the lower third.

The meridian hatch lines are much fainter and thinner than the bold, closely-spaced orange meridians that cover the left half of the source drawing, so the characteristic 'ruled surface' look is weakened.
An extra blue interactive chord plus '60.0 m' readout sits beside the printed black '60 m' dimension, duplicating the waist annotation in the default state (not in the source).
The source's lower horizontal ledge/skirt line across the base of the shell is not clearly reproduced as a distinct drawn line.
